1_persistent_variables.method: AST — variables assigned inside the loop but initialised before it

FIVE_STRUCTURAL_QUESTIONS.2_state_changing_predicates: trig = any_vol = abs_sig | climb_sig | load_sig; on trig, latch (h[i], l[i], i)

3_reset_conditional_or_unconditional.guard: not isnan(cur_h) AND i > cur_bar AND since > _BREAK_BARS
3_reset_conditional_or_unconditional.KEY_FINDING: the guard depends only on cur_bar and i — NEVER on unknown upstream data. This is what makes the reset a genuine identifiability anchor rather than a mere counter.
3_reset_conditional_or_unconditional.CAVEAT: 'if trig[i]' executes FIRST, so an UNKNOWN trigger can re-latch and postpone the reset. Convergence therefore requires trig PROVEN FALSE across the window, not merely unobserved.

4_reset_determines_output_or_only_next_s.evidence: the else-branch emits no output, so vbo_up[i] stays FALSE, AND clears the latch
4_reset_determines_output_or_only_next_s.also: on the latch bar itself i > cur_bar is False, so the trigger bar's own output is FALSE

5_load_sig_cooldown_entry.asymmetry: load_sig is PROVEN FALSE whenever load_base is FALSE, regardless of cooldown state
5_load_sig_cooldown_entry.consequence: cooldown ambiguity can make trig UNKNOWN only when load_base is TRUE AND abs_sig and climb_sig are both FALSE — a strictly narrower condition than it first appears

RESET_OFFSET_EXACT.rule: reset fires at EXACTLY latch_index + 11 (the 11th bar AFTER the latch bar)
RESET_OFFSET_EXACT.gap_reading: if the latch is the last bar before a gap, recovery lands on the 11th OBSERVED bar
RESET_OFFSET_EXACT.correction: an earlier fixture printed 12 because the latch bar was itself counted in K; the offset is 11

TWO_COLLAPSE_MECHANISMS.immediate: a PROVEN trigger collapses any admissible state set to a singleton latch at that bar
TWO_COLLAPSE_MECHANISMS.finite: 11 consecutive bars with trig PROVEN FALSE after the latch collapse all states to NONE
TWO_COLLAPSE_MECHANISMS.answer_to_the_key_question: YES — for all admissible prior states, the _BREAK_BARS condition yields an identical next state, because the reset guard reads only state and index. _BREAK_BARS IS an identifiability bound here, not merely a window parameter.

FIXTURES.F1_F4_boundary: latch@j: not converged at j+10, converged at j+11 — boundary is exact
FIXTURES.F2_unknown_not_false: 12 UNKNOWN-trigger bars -> 12 reachable states; 12 PROVEN-FALSE bars -> 1. Coercing UNKNOWN to FALSE would collapse 12 states to 1.
FIXTURES.F3_reset_bar: proven trigger collapses {None,0,1,2}+5 unknown bars (6 states) to the singleton {5}
FIXTURES.F5_load_cooldown: propagates into trig only under the narrow condition above
FIXTURES.F6_contaminated_gap: state branches; recovery is event-anchored, verified exactly

REDUCTION_vs_exact_simulator.oracle_note: state-set comparison is the PRIMARY oracle; output equality alone would be vacuous for a rare boolean

OPEN_DECISION_TRIGGER_DEPTH.why_they_differ: _atr uses ewm (infinite impulse response), so it never converges EXACTLY — 'stable-from age 60' is float-equality convergence, not a hard window
OPEN_DECISION_TRIGGER_DEPTH.precedent: the user previously ruled APPROVE age>=14 -> VALID for rsi_14 and Massive ATR14, accepting the asymptotic nature of Wilder ewm
OPEN_DECISION_TRIGGER_DEPTH.WHY_NOT_ASSUMED: extending that ruling to the vbo_up trigger is an INFERENCE, not a covered case. No tolerance may be invented, so this is surfaced rather than decided.
